capabilities.label: Saying it does not know
capabilities.summary: Covers detecting unanswerable or underspecified problems and gaps between what hidden states encode and what the model asserts; excludes ordinary accuracy on solvable problems.

best_supports.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
best_supports.finding: Anthropic's self-knowledge study shows large models are well-calibrated on multiple-choice/true-false questions and can self-evaluate open-ended answers via P(True), with performance and calibration improving with scale and with exposure to multiple sampled candidates. Models can also be trained to predict P(IK), the probability they know an answer without seeing a proposed answer, which responds appropriately to relevant source material or hints in context and partially generalizes across tasks, though calibration degrades on new tasks. This establishes knowing-what-you-know as a measurable capability separable from raw task accuracy — the model can be wrong yet correctly signal low confidence — directly supporting abstention and self-knowledge as a distinct axis to track.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Know What They Don't Know?
papers.finding: Introduces SelfAware, a benchmark of unanswerable questions across five categories paired with answerable counterparts, and an automated uncertainty-detection method; across 20 LLMs (GPT-3, InstructGPT, LLaMA families) models show a measurable intrinsic capacity to recognize unanswerable questions that grows with scale, in-context learning, and instruction tuning, yet still falls well short of human performance. This establishes abstention/self-knowledge as a separately measurable axis distinct from accuracy on answerable questions.

papers.title: R-Tuning: Instructing Large Language Models to Say `I Don't Know'
papers.finding: R-Tuning constructs refusal-aware instruction data from the gap between a model's parametric knowledge and the tuning data, and shows models can be taught to answer known questions while declining unknown ones. The refusal ability generalizes to out-of-domain datasets as a 'meta-skill', and learning to express uncertainty improves calibration — evidence that abstention/self-knowledge is a separable, trainable capability rather than a byproduct of task accuracy.

papers.title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
papers.finding: A dedicated survey frames abstention as a distinct, tractable research area, organizing methods, benchmarks, and metrics around query-, model-, and human-value-based reasons to refuse, and explicitly motivates studying abstention as a meta-capability that transcends specific tasks or domains. This directly supports treating abstention/self-knowledge as a separable capability rather than a byproduct of task accuracy, though as a survey it contributes synthesis rather than new measurement.

papers.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations via Conformal Abstention
papers.finding: The paper builds a conformal-prediction abstention procedure that uses self-consistency plus LLM self-evaluation of response similarity to decide when the model should say "I don't know", and shows it bounds the hallucination rate with theoretical guarantees while abstaining less often than log-probability baselines on long-answer tasks (Temporal Sequences) and comparably on TriviaQA. This treats abstention as a separately measurable, tunable axis distinct from raw answer accuracy: the trade-off curve between abstention rate and error rate is the object of study, and models differ in how well their internal confidence signals support it.

capabilities.label: Giving a useful assessment of someone else's work
capabilities.summary: Whether a model's evaluation of an artifact agrees with careful human judgement and says something actionable; the failures are bias toward surface features, agreement with the author, and critique that sounds specific but is not.

best_supports.title: Evaluating Judges as Evaluators: The JETTS Benchmark of LLM-as-Judges as Test-Time Scaling Evaluators
best_supports.finding: JETTS evaluates 10 LLM-judges (7B–70B) as evaluators for 8 generators across math, code, and instruction following in three settings: reranking, beam search, and critique-based refinement. Judges are competitive with outcome reward models at reranking but consistently worse than process reward models in beam search, and—most directly relevant—their natural-language critiques largely fail to improve the generator's subsequent responses, with refinement often leaving quality flat or degrading it and judges frequently failing to identify which responses need revision. This isolates critique quality (does the assessment say something actionable that improves downstream work) as a measurable axis that is separable from raw preference-ranking accuracy, since the same judges that rank reasonably still produce unhelpful critiques.

papers.title: Evaluating Judges as Evaluators: The JETTS Benchmark of LLM-as-Judges as Test-Time Scaling Evaluators
papers.finding: JETTS evaluates 10 LLM-judges (7B–70B) as evaluators for 8 generators across math, code, and instruction following in three settings: reranking, beam search, and critique-based refinement. papers.title: UXBench: Measuring the Actionability of LLM-Generated UX Critiques
papers.finding: UXBench evaluates eight frontier models as UX judges, scoring their critiques by whether a fixed downstream repair agent can actually improve the interface, plus a blind human validation study. Models differ meaningfully in report actionability, show distinct rubric-level repair signatures, vary in fixture-level reliability, and trade leadership across product-surface categories — evidence that critique quality is a real, non-saturated, multi-dimensional axis separable from general capability.

papers.title: Large language models as judges: recent advances in LLM-based evaluation, critique, preference modeling, and feedback for text and code
papers.finding: A survey of LLM-as-judge work (2020–early 2026) that treats evaluation, critique, and preference modeling as a coherent research area, builds a taxonomy of judging tasks across text and code, and documents systematic biases (length, position, self-preference) plus agreement-with-human-judgement as the central quality metric. It supports the capability as a real, distinct construct, though as a secondary synthesis rather than new measurement, and much of its bias discussion overlaps judge-position-bias and sycophancy.

papers.title: RefineCoder: Iterative Improving of Large Language Models via Adaptive Critique Refinement for Code Generation
papers.finding: RefineCoder uses an LLM-as-a-Judge scoring system plus an LLM-as-a-Critic that writes critiques of self-generated low-quality code, and shows that training on critique-guided refinements yields continuous gains across code benchmarks with less data than distillation baselines. This is evidence that model critique can be actionable enough to improve subsequent output quality, the downstream half of the proposed capability, though the paper does not validate critique quality against careful human judgement or isolate critique from the scoring/selection pipeline.

capabilities.label: Handling culture-specific norms and viewpoints
capabilities.summary: Covers implicit cultural norms, dialects, local pragmatics, and representing the spread of a population's views; excludes general multilingual fluency or factual trivia about cultures.

best_supports.title: CultureConverse: A Multilingual Multi-turn Simulation Harness for Culturally Grounded Assistance in East and Southeast Asia
best_supports.finding: CultureConverse argues that existing cultural evaluations collapse culture into single-turn factual MCQ recall, and builds a multilingual multi-turn simulation harness across 10 East/Southeast Asian regions, 58 subgroup identities, and 7 domains in which the assistant must infer implicit cultural constraints while giving practical help. Treating this as a distinct measurement target — separate from factual trivia about cultures and from multilingual fluency — directly supports cultural competence as its own trackable capability, and the subgroup-level breakdown speaks to representing within-population variation.

papers.title: CultureConverse: A Multilingual Multi-turn Simulation Harness for Culturally Grounded Assistance in East and Southeast Asia

capabilities.label: Finding and fixing a fault in existing code
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can localise the cause of a failing behaviour in code it did not just write and repair it without breaking something else; distinct from generating code and from self-repair of its own output.

best_supports.title: A Survey of Learning-based Automated Program Repair
best_supports.finding: A systematic survey of learning-based automated program repair treats bug fixing in existing code as its own research field with a distinct pipeline — fault localisation, patch generation, patch ranking, patch validation, and patch correctness assessment — plus dedicated benchmarks (e.g. Defects4J-style datasets) and metrics separate from code-generation evaluation. The explicit separation of fault localisation from patch generation, and of plausible from correct patches (patch overfitting, i.e. fixes that pass tests but break other behaviour), backs the claim that repairing code the model did not author is a measurable capability distinct from generating code from a specification. As a survey it reports no new head-to-head measurement, so the support is organisational rather than experimental.

papers.title: A Survey of Learning-based Automated Program Repair
papers.finding: A systematic survey of learning-based automated program repair treats bug fixing in existing code as its own research field with a distinct pipeline — fault localisation, patch generation, patch ranking, patch validation, and patch correctness assessment — plus dedicated benchmarks (e.g. Defects4J-style datasets) and metrics separate from code-generation evaluation. papers.title: Explainable automated debugging via large language model-driven scientific debugging
papers.finding: AutoSD prompts LLMs to iteratively form hypotheses, run a debugger on pre-existing buggy programs from standard APR benchmarks (e.g. Defects4J-style suites), and then produce patches plus human-readable rationales. It performs competitively with program repair baselines and can signal when it is confident; a 20-participant study found explanations improved developers' accuracy in judging patch correctness on five of six real bugs. This treats fault localisation and repair of third-party buggy code as a measurable capability distinct from generating code from a spec or fixing one's own draft.

papers.title: Adversarial Testing of Automated Program Repair Agents for Security Vulnerabilities
papers.finding: The paper studies LLM-based automated program repair agents fixing bugs in code they did not author, and shows that adversarially-phrased but benign-looking issue reports can steer agents into producing functionally correct but insecure patches. This treats repair of third-party faulty code as a measurable behaviour with its own failure modes (correct fix, broken security), supporting debugging as a distinct capability while also implicating secure-coding and prompt-injection-like manipulation.

papers.title: LLMs in Software Security: A Survey of Vulnerability Detection Techniques and Insights
papers.finding: A survey of LLM-based vulnerability detection and repair suggestion in existing code. It documents an active literature on localising faults (security defects) in code the model did not author, plus repair generation, and catalogues datasets, metrics and challenges such as repository-level analysis and false positives. As a survey it offers no new measurement, and its framing centres on security vulnerabilities rather than general behavioural bug localisation and fix, so it only weakly bears on debugging as a distinct tracked capability.

capabilities.label: Competence in a specialist domain
capabilities.summary: Whether a general model performs like a practitioner in a specific field (medicine, law, hardware design, a scientific subfield), and where the general-purpose competence stops.

best_supports.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge
best_supports.finding: Med-PaLM/Flan-PaLM reach state-of-the-art on medical multiple-choice benchmarks (67.6% on MedQA) yet human expert evaluation along factuality, reasoning, harm and bias axes shows the general instruction-tuned model lags clinicians substantially — e.g. scientific-consensus alignment and low-harm rates far below physician answers — with domain-specific instruction prompt tuning closing much but not all of the gap. This is direct evidence that specialist-domain competence is a separable, measurable axis that general-purpose benchmarks overstate.

papers.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge
papers.finding: Med-PaLM/Flan-PaLM reach state-of-the-art on medical multiple-choice benchmarks (67.6% on MedQA) yet human expert evaluation along factuality, reasoning, harm and bias axes shows the general instruction-tuned model lags clinicians substantially — e.g. scientific-consensus alignment and low-harm rates far below physician answers — with domain-specific instruction prompt tuning closing much but not all of the gap. papers.title: Performance of ChatGPT on USMLE: Potential for AI-assisted medical education using large language models
papers.finding: ChatGPT, with no medical fine-tuning, scored at or near the passing threshold on all three USMLE steps and produced explanations rated high in concordance and insight, establishing that a general model's medical competence can be measured against the practitioner-licensing bar and located just at its edge. The result both validates domain competence as a trackable axis and marks where general-purpose knowledge stops short of comfortable expert performance.

capabilities.label: Acting on an environment and reading what came back
capabilities.summary: Whether an agent can take actions in a digital environment — a browser, a shell, a game, an operating system — observe the result, and update what it does next; the failure is acting on a stale or misread state.

best_supports.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
best_supports.finding: ReAct evaluates LLMs acting in interactive environments (ALFWorld text world, WebShop, a Wikipedia search API) where each observation depends on the prior action, and shows that interleaving reasoning with actions raises success rates by 34% (ALFWorld) and 10% (WebShop) over imitation/RL baselines with only one or two in-context examples. It also documents the characteristic failure mode: act-only agents misread or fail to update on returned observations, while reason-only (CoT) agents hallucinate facts because they never observe the environment at all. This is direct evidence that acting-and-observing is a measurable, separable ability distinct from static reasoning, though the paper frames it as a prompting method rather than a capability taxonomy, and two of its four tasks (HotpotQA, Fever) are closer to retrieval-augmented QA than genuine environment interaction.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

papers.title: InterCode: Standardizing and Benchmarking Interactive Coding with Execution Feedback
papers.finding: InterCode frames interactive coding as an RL environment where code is the action and execution feedback is the observation, and shows that LLMs given execution feedback across Bash, SQL, and Python environments perform substantially differently (and generally better with interaction) than in static single-shot generation — while still failing on multi-turn tasks like Capture the Flag that require adapting to returned state. This is direct evidence that acting-and-observing in an environment is a separable, measurable skill beyond static code generation.

papers.title: Adaptation of Agentic AI: A Survey of Post-Training, Memory, and Skills
papers.finding: A survey of agent adaptation methods that treats environment-grounded action as a first-class setting, reviewing evaluation practices across deep research, software development, and computer use — domains where the agent acts and observes results. It organizes adaptation paradigms around tool-execution signals, implying that feedback from acting on an environment is a distinct learning and evaluation surface. As a survey it offers framing rather than new measurement, and it mostly folds environment interaction into broader notions of tool use and adaptation, so it is only weak support for treating the capability as separately trackable.

papers.title: Personal LLM Agents: Insights and Survey about the Capability, Efficiency and Security
papers.finding: A survey/vision paper on Personal LLM Agents that discusses architecture, task automation on devices, tool use and UI operation as key capabilities, but presents no measurements of agents acting in an environment and reading back observations. It offers conceptual framing rather than evidence bearing on whether environment interaction is a distinct, measurable capability.

capabilities.label: Spotting an error in a given artifact
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can find the mistake in something put in front of it — a proof, a program, an argument, a table — when told there may be one; distinct from fixing it, and from judging overall quality.

best_supports.title: Effective test generation using pre-trained Large Language Models and mutation testing
best_supports.finding: MuTAP evaluates LLM-generated unit tests by their ability to expose bugs in code the model did not write, reporting detection of up to 28% more faulty human-written snippets than baselines and a 93.57% mutation score on synthetic buggy code — an indirect but concrete measurement of error-finding in given artifacts. The paper also shows plain LLM prompting produces tests that miss certain bug types and corner cases, requiring mutation-guided prompt augmentation, which supports treating error detection as a separable, non-trivial ability rather than a byproduct of code generation. Evidence is mediated through test generation rather than direct error localization, so it speaks to the capability only obliquely.

papers.finding: MuTAP evaluates LLM-generated unit tests by their ability to expose bugs in code the model did not write, reporting detection of up to 28% more faulty human-written snippets than baselines and a 93.57% mutation score on synthetic buggy code — an indirect but concrete measurement of error-finding in given artifacts. The paper also shows plain LLM prompting produces tests that miss certain bug types and corner cases, requiring mutation-guided prompt augmentation, which supports treating error detection as a separable, non-trivial ability rather than a byproduct of code generation. Evidence is mediated through test generation rather than direct error localization, so it speaks to the capability only obliquely.

papers.title: Large Language Model for Vulnerability Detection and Repair: Literature Review and the Road Ahead
papers.finding: A systematic literature review of 58 papers on LLMs for vulnerability detection and repair, which treats detection (finding a vulnerability in code the model did not write) as a separate task from repair, with its own body of adaptation techniques (fine-tuning, prompting, retrieval) and benchmarks. This organizational split corroborates that spotting an error in a given artifact is tracked independently of fixing it, though as a survey it contributes no new measurements of detection precision/recall itself, and covers only the security-vulnerability slice of the capability.

capabilities.label: Recalling facts it was trained on
capabilities.summary: Whether a model retrieves a fact from its weights when asked, especially long-tail facts; the failure is a wrong or missing answer, measured against ground truth, not the confidence of a made-up one.

best_supports.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge
best_supports.finding: Med-PaLM/Flan-PaLM evaluations on MultiMedQA measure closed-book medical knowledge recall against ground-truth answers, and the authors report that knowledge recall (scored as a separate axis in human evaluation alongside comprehension and reasoning) improves with model scale and instruction prompt tuning — treating parametric factual recall as a distinct, measurable, scale-dependent ability. Flan-PaLM reaches 67.6% on MedQA, yet human raters still find factual gaps relative to clinicians, showing recall remains imperfect on specialized long-tail content. Evidence is indirect for the frequency/popularity framing, since the paper varies model size and tuning rather than fact frequency.

papers.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge

capabilities.label: Retaining skills and safety after fine-tuning
capabilities.summary: Covers loss of general capability, out-of-domain skill, or refusal behavior caused by domain, multimodal, or alignment fine-tuning; excludes in-domain accuracy gains and inference-time behavior shifts.

best_supports.title: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
best_supports.finding: Across 21 instruction-tuned models (3B-32B, six alignment recipes), refusal behavior is shown to sit in a low-rank 'safety subspace' that small-scale benign LoRA fine-tuning can erase; ablating directions in this subspace causally weakens refusal, and a pre-fine-tuning Geometric Fragility Score predicts which initially-safe model retains the most refusal after fine-tuning. This treats post-fine-tuning safety retention as a measurable, model-varying property distinct from release-time refusal test performance.

papers.title: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
papers.finding: Across 21 instruction-tuned models (3B-32B, six alignment recipes), refusal behavior is shown to sit in a low-rank 'safety subspace' that small-scale benign LoRA fine-tuning can erase; ablating directions in this subspace causally weakens refusal, and a pre-fine-tuning Geometric Fragility Score predicts which initially-safe model retains the most refusal after fine-tuning. This treats post-fine-tuning safety retention as a measurable, model-varying property distinct from release-time refusal test performance.

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
papers.finding: The paper documents exactly the failure mode the capability describes: fine-tuning on downstream corpora can strip or subvert safety alignment, and existing realignment defenses restore refusal behavior only at the cost of catastrophic forgetting of specialized skills. Across three datasets and three base models with varying alignment strength, baseline defenses show severe downstream task degradation under prompt-template mismatch, while the proposed ROPD method preserves both refusal robustness and capability. This treats safety/capability retention after fine-tuning as a measurable, jointly-tracked axis distinct from in-domain accuracy.

papers.title: More Than Catastrophic Forgetting: Integrating General Capabilities For Domain-Specific LLMs
papers.finding: The paper takes catastrophic forgetting after domain fine-tuning as an established starting point and argues it is insufficient: legal-domain fine-tuned LLMs must also integrate general capabilities with domain knowledge within single instances (General Capabilities Integration). It constructs three groups of legal training/testing tasks and shows standard LoRA fine-tuning struggles, while an attention-augmented ALoRA better switches between domain and general competencies. This is evidence that loss/degradation of general skills from domain fine-tuning is a real, separately measurable failure mode, though the paper's emphasis shifts toward integration rather than pure retention, and evidence is single-domain (legal).

papers.title: Unlearners Can Lie: Evaluating and Improving Honesty in LLM Unlearning
papers.finding: Evaluating 9 unlearning methods across 3 families, the paper finds that post-hoc weight updates intended to remove specific knowledge systematically damage retained-set utility and honesty, inducing hallucination, abnormal token sequences, and inconsistent refusal behavior — collateral degradation of general capability and refusal reliability from targeted fine-tuning. Their ReVa representation-alignment fine-tune shows the damage is partly recoverable, implying it is a measurable, addressable property rather than an inherent cost. This is evidence that side effects of fine-tuning on retained skills and safety behavior are a distinct axis worth tracking, though the setting is unlearning rather than domain or multimodal adaptation.

capabilities.label: Formalizing and machine-checking mathematics
capabilities.summary: Covers autoformalization into a solver-checkable language, producing proof-assistant-verified proofs, and localizing the first flawed step in a proof; excludes informal math word problems.

best_supports.title: Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations
best_supports.finding: AlphaGeometry pairs a from-scratch language model with a symbolic deduction engine to produce machine-checkable, human-readable proofs for olympiad Euclidean geometry, solving 25/30 recent IMO-level problems versus 10 for the prior best method and approaching IMO gold-medallist level. The paper explicitly frames the bottleneck as the cost of translating human proofs into machine-verifiable format (autoformalization), and addresses it with millions of synthesized theorem-proof pairs, treating verified formal proof generation as a distinct target separate from informal math problem solving.

papers.title: Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations
papers.finding: AlphaGeometry pairs a from-scratch language model with a symbolic deduction engine to produce machine-checkable, human-readable proofs for olympiad Euclidean geometry, solving 25/30 recent IMO-level problems versus 10 for the prior best method and approaching IMO gold-medallist level. capabilities.label: Writing a reusable locator: regex, SQL, XPath
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can turn an intent or a few examples into a regex, SQL query, XPath or jq path that selects the right subset, so the pattern can run over the whole collection without calling the model again.

best_supports.title: Neural Generation of Regular Expressions from Natural Language with Minimal Domain Knowledge
best_supports.finding: Introduces NL-RX-Turk, a large parallel corpus of natural-language descriptions paired with regular expressions, and shows a plain seq2seq model translating intent into regex artefacts evaluated by DFA-equivalence (functional match, not string match), beating prior semantic-parsing baselines by 19.6%. This establishes NL-to-pattern-language synthesis as a separately measurable task with its own dataset and correctness criterion, distinct from generic program synthesis, and its far-from-ceiling accuracy shows the skill is non-trivial.

papers.title: Neural Generation of Regular Expressions from Natural Language with Minimal Domain Knowledge
papers.finding: Introduces NL-RX-Turk, a large parallel corpus of natural-language descriptions paired with regular expressions, and shows a plain seq2seq model translating intent into regex artefacts evaluated by DFA-equivalence (functional match, not string match), beating prior semantic-parsing baselines by 19.6%. This establishes NL-to-pattern-language synthesis as a separately measurable task with its own dataset and correctness criterion, distinct from generic program synthesis, and its far-from-ceiling accuracy shows the skill is non-trivial.

papers.title: From Examples to Patterns: LLM-Generated Regular Expressions for Entity Extraction in Czech Clinical Texts
papers.finding: The paper has LLMs synthesize regular expressions from a handful of labelled examples of clinical entities in Czech notes, then refines them with a feedback loop, and scores the emitted patterns by how well they match held-out targets. LLM-generated regexes beat state-of-the-art genetic-programming regex induction, especially in the few-example regime. This is exactly the proposed capability: the artefact produced is a reusable pattern that runs over the whole corpus without further model calls, and it is measured on selection correctness rather than on downstream extraction done by the model itself. It also shows the task is separately measurable and non-trivial (regex expressiveness limits the entity types where the approach works), supporting treatment as a distinct capability.

papers.title: Spider: A Large-Scale Human-Labeled Dataset for Complex and Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL Task
papers.finding: Spider frames text-to-SQL as its own task: 10,181 questions paired with 5,693 complex SQL queries over 200 multi-table databases, with train/test splits on unseen databases so models must emit a query that generalizes rather than recall a memorized program. Evaluation is exact-set matching plus execution against the database, i.e. whether the emitted pattern selects the right rows, not whether the model answers the question directly. The best model of the time reached only 12.4% exact match on the database split, establishing formal-query synthesis as a distinct and then-unsolved capability separable from general code generation.

papers.title: A Survey of Text-to-SQL in the Era of LLMs: Where are we, and where are we going?
papers.finding: A comprehensive survey of LLM-based Text-to-SQL covering models, training/synthetic data, benchmarks, evaluation metrics (e.g. execution accuracy, exact-set match) and error taxonomies. The existence of a distinct, heavily-benchmarked research area whose output is a reusable query-language artefact judged by whether it selects the right rows supports treating formal-query synthesis as a separable capability with its own failure modes (schema linking, NL ambiguity/under-specification) rather than an instance of general code generation. Caveat: it is a survey covering only SQL, not regex/XPath/jq, so it evidences one member of the proposed family rather than the family as a whole.

papers.title: SemRegex: A Semantics-Based Approach for Generating Regular Expressions from Natural Language Specifications
papers.finding: SemRegex targets NL-to-regex generation and argues that syntactic match is the wrong yardstick: semantically equivalent regexes take many syntactic forms, so it evaluates and trains against DFA-equivalence and test-case-based semantic correctness, improving over MLE seq2seq baselines on three public datasets (KB13, NL-Turk, NL-RX). This is direct evidence that emitting a reusable pattern-language artefact judged by what it matches is a distinct, measurable skill separate from generic code generation scored by token overlap.

capabilities.label: Improving its own scaffolding from failures
capabilities.summary: Whether an agent system can read its own failure traces and rewrite the prompts, tools and policies it runs inside so later runs do better, with no person making the edit.

best_supports.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
best_supports.finding: The paper treats self-evolving runtime harnesses — agent systems that revise their own harness code from execution feedback — as an established paradigm worth optimizing, and proposes Ecdysis to train such harnesses more efficiently while avoiding overfitting to observed failure patterns. Its framing presupposes and its evaluation measures before-and-after task performance from automated harness edits, which is exactly the proposed capability; the critique it raises (search cost, overfitting to specific failure traces, degraded generalization) is a critique of existing methods' efficiency, not of the capability's existence or distinctness.

papers.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
papers.finding: The paper treats self-evolving runtime harnesses — agent systems that revise their own harness code from execution feedback — as an established paradigm worth optimizing, and proposes Ecdysis to train such harnesses more efficiently while avoiding overfitting to observed failure patterns. Its framing presupposes and its evaluation measures before-and-after task performance from automated harness edits, which is exactly the proposed capability; the critique it raises (search cost, overfitting to specific failure traces, degraded generalization) is a critique of existing methods' efficiency, not of the capability's existence or distinctness.

papers.title: HypoForge: A Self-Improving Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Hypothesis Generation and Testing via Scientific Skill Learning
papers.finding: HypoForge is a multi-agent scientific-discovery system that accumulates reusable 'skills' from its own run traces—adversarial critique signals for hypothesis generation and execution feedback for hypothesis testing—and writes them back into its own workflow, with reported gains over static-prompt / fixed-workflow baselines. That is exactly the self-editing-scaffold loop the capability describes: no human edits the prompts or procedures between runs, and improvement is measured before-and-after on downstream tasks. Evidence is domain-specific (hypothesis generation/testing) and the abstract is truncated before the numbers, so it is supporting rather than decisive, and self-improvement is confounded with the multi-agent design.

papers.title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi Agent Systems
papers.finding: AgentGrad is a textual-gradient method in which a multi-agent system uses its own failure traces to identify which agent's prompt caused the failure and rewrite it, with before-and-after task scores; this is exactly the loop of a system editing its own scaffolding from traces, and its diagnosis of failure modes in gradient extraction and aggregation shows the capability is non-trivial and separable from single-output self-repair.

papers.title: Experience Funnel: A State-Policy Alternating Loop for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.finding: The paper's premise is that agents can distill their own interaction experience into explicit, editable textual states (skills, agent harnesses) that improve later behavior, then alternately fold those states into parametric policies. The explicit-state half of the loop is exactly self-editing scaffolding evaluated with before-and-after task performance, so it treats harness self-improvement as a real, separable mechanism — though the paper deliberately blends it with weight-level updating, which sits outside the proposed scope and blurs the boundary.

papers.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
papers.finding: Reports a self-evolving agent framework that detects its own low-consistency failure modes on AppWorld and revises its operating scaffolding to narrow a measured 24-point gap between per-run pass rate (77%) and pass-all-5 consistency (53%), giving a before-and-after on the same tasks without human edits — evidence that automated harness self-improvement is a separately measurable capability. Strength limited by single-benchmark scope and a truncated abstract that does not specify exactly which artifacts (prompts, memory, tools) are rewritten.

capabilities.label: Refusing harmful requests under obfuscation
capabilities.summary: Covers maintaining refusal when harmful intent is wrapped in roleplay or encodings, harm that emerges only from combined segments, and unsafe content inside reasoning traces; excludes instructions injected via retrieved data.

best_supports.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
best_supports.finding: The paper documents that harmful prompts wrapped in complex framings (roleplay-style 'undercover' wrappers) defeat existing SAE steering safety controls, and introduces GUISE, a dedicated benchmark of wrapper-obfuscated harmful prompts, plus a steering method (REINS) aimed at restoring refusal. This treats robustness of refusal under obfuscation as a separately measurable failure mode distinct from plain harmful-request refusal.

papers.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
papers.finding: The paper documents that harmful prompts wrapped in complex framings (roleplay-style 'undercover' wrappers) defeat existing SAE steering safety controls, and introduces GUISE, a dedicated benchmark of wrapper-obfuscated harmful prompts, plus a steering method (REINS) aimed at restoring refusal. This treats robustness of refusal under obfuscation as a separately measurable failure mode distinct from plain harmful-request refusal.

papers.title: A survey of safety and trustworthiness of large language models through the lens of verification and validation
papers.finding: This broad V&V survey catalogues LLM vulnerabilities including jailbreak and prompt-based attacks that elicit harmful outputs despite safety alignment, treating robustness to such attacks as a distinct safety property requiring dedicated falsification, evaluation, and runtime monitoring. It is corroborating background rather than direct evidence: it reports no new measurements of obfuscated-harm refusal, and jailbreaking is only one item among many (hallucination, privacy, backdoors, fairness) in its taxonomy.

papers.title: AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.finding: This broad alignment survey catalogues adversarial robustness and 'jailbreak'/red-teaming failures as a recognized research area, treating resistance to adversarial prompting as a distinct assurance target under its Robustness principle. It is a secondary overview rather than direct measurement, so it corroborates the capability's existence and importance without providing new evidence of its distinctness from related safety behaviors.

capabilities.label: Absorbing and flexibly using new knowledge
capabilities.summary: Covers whether newly injected or post-training facts can be recalled under paraphrase, combined, and used to override stale beliefs; excludes retrieval-based grounding at inference time.

best_supports.title: Popular Knowledge Propagates More Errors in LLM Knowledge Updating
best_supports.finding: The paper studies fine-tuning-based knowledge updating directly, showing that injecting new facts causes collateral corruption of already-encoded facts — and that popular (head) knowledge propagates more errors than long-tail knowledge. This documents a distinct failure mode of absorbing new knowledge without retrieval, supporting the capability as a real, separately measurable axis (update success vs. forgetting/hallucination side effects).

papers.title: Popular Knowledge Propagates More Errors in LLM Knowledge Updating

papers.title: From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection
papers.finding: The paper frames continual knowledge injection as a distinct problem where SFT-injected facts are memorized in training format but fail to transfer to paraphrases, multi-document combinations, and downstream reasoning — exactly the recall-under-paraphrase-and-composition distinction the capability describes. Its proposed mixed-policy RL method (GRIN) is motivated by and evaluated against this generalization gap, treating 'memorization' versus 'absorption' as separable measurable behaviors, which supports tracking knowledge updating as a real capability rather than a byproduct of general factual accuracy or retrieval.

papers.title: Synthetic Worlds for Temporal Evaluation and Knowledge Updating in LLMs
papers.finding: The paper builds ParallelEvents, a synthetic benchmark of fictional-but-plausible future worlds with coherent event trajectories, explicitly to measure knowledge insertion and updating in LLMs without contamination or the counterfactual-conflict problems of prior edit benchmarks. Constructing a dedicated, contamination-controlled evaluation for absorbing and using newly injected post-training facts treats knowledge updating as a distinct, measurable capability rather than a byproduct of general factual recall. The synthetic-world design also isolates the failure mode where models must override stale or conflicting priors, which is the core of the proposed capability.

capabilities.label: Deducing validly from logical structure
capabilities.summary: Covers strict rule-based deduction, stability under label-preserving rephrasings, and retracting conclusions when evidence changes; excludes arithmetic and factual QA.

best_supports.title: Fundamental Capabilities and Applications of Large Language Models: A Survey
best_supports.finding: This broad survey of LLM fundamental capabilities enumerates reasoning — including logical/deductive reasoning — as a distinct fundamental capability with its own definition, formation mechanism, and evaluation strategy, separate from knowledge/factual recall, mathematical computation, and generation abilities. That taxonomy lends general, if indirect, support to treating rule-based deduction as a trackable capability. However, the survey is a high-level overview and provides no targeted evidence on the specific facets the proposal emphasizes — stability under label-preserving rephrasings and non-monotonic retraction when evidence changes — so it corroborates the category's existence more than its robustness framing.

capabilities.label: Getting more from several models than from one
capabilities.summary: Whether a system of several models or agents — debating, voting, dividing work, or sharing state — does better than its best single member; the failure is a quorum of copies that agree on the same mistake.

best_supports.title: Enhancing diagnostic capability with multi-agents conversational large language models
best_supports.finding: A Multi-Agent Conversation framework (four doctor agents plus a supervisor, GPT-4 base) outperformed single-model GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on diagnosis and test recommendation across 302 rare disease cases, and also beat Chain-of-Thought, Self-Refine, and Self-Consistency baselines, with agent count and roles mattering for performance. This is direct evidence that the combination rule — not just extra sampling or self-verification — produces the gain, though the token-count confound and single narrow domain limit strength.

papers.title: Enhancing diagnostic capability with multi-agents conversational large language models

This is direct evidence that the combination rule — not just extra sampling or self-verification — produces the gain, though the token-count confound and single narrow domain limit strength.

papers.title: A survey on LLM-based multi-agent systems: workflow, infrastructure, and challenges
papers.finding: A survey of LLM-based multi-agent systems that organizes the field around profile, perception, self-action, mutual interaction, and evolution, and catalogues applications in problem-solving and world simulation. It establishes that combining multiple LLM agents via communication and coordination is a distinct and active research area, and flags open challenges (e.g., coordination overhead, evaluation), but it presents no new measurement of multi-agent systems against single-model baselines, so it corroborates the category rather than evidencing a gain.

papers.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering: Literature Review, Vision, and the Road Ahead
papers.finding: A systematic literature review of LLM-based multi-agent systems across the software development lifecycle, plus two case studies of state-of-the-art LMA frameworks, arguing that collaboration and specialization among multiple agents improve robustness and scalability over single-agent approaches while identifying gaps in agent synergy. It treats multi-agent combination as a distinct object of study, but as a survey it offers little controlled head-to-head measurement against single-model baselines, so it is weak direct evidence.

papers.title: Large Language Model Enhanced Multi-Agent Systems for 6G Communications
papers.finding: Proposes CommLLM, a three-stage multi-agent pipeline (multi-agent data retrieval, collaborative planning by several planning agents with different perspectives, and evaluation/reflection/refinement agents) for 6G communication tasks, and reports in a semantic-communication design case study that the agentic system produces workable solutions where a native single LLM fails due to missing domain knowledge and weak reasoning/self-evaluation. Evidence is a single domain-specific demonstration in a magazine-style paper rather than a controlled benchmark with ablations isolating the contribution of multiplicity versus retrieval and tools, so it supports the capability's existence only weakly and does not probe the correlated-error failure mode.

capabilities.label: Carrying a chain of inference through to its conclusion
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can hold several dependent inference steps and reach the conclusion they entail, as opposed to pattern-matching the answer; failures show as correct steps with a wrong join, or shortcuts.

best_supports.title: Theseus in the Graph: Towards Traceable Multi-Hop Graph Navigation
best_supports.finding: The paper re-frames multi-hop KGQA as question-conditioned graph navigation (THESEUS) precisely because existing systems predict final answers without modeling or validating intermediate hops, leaving it unclear whether correct answers come from faithful multi-hop reasoning or shortcuts. By making each hop an explicit, traceable step, it treats step-wise inference as the object of measurement rather than the final answer, which is the core distinction the capability draws. It is a method/benchmark-framing contribution rather than a controlled study varying hop count, so it supports the capability's reality without quantifying accuracy decay per dependent step.

papers.title: Theseus in the Graph: Towards Traceable Multi-Hop Graph Navigation

capabilities.label: Performing evenly across languages
capabilities.summary: Covers gaps between high- and low-resource languages on identical tasks, including uneven parametric knowledge coverage by region; excludes translation quality per se.

best_supports.title: A survey of multilingual large language models
best_supports.finding: This survey of multilingual LLMs organizes the field around multilingual alignment and explicitly frames cross-lingual performance imbalance — strong results in high-resource languages versus weak coverage of low-resource ones — as a core open challenge motivating dedicated methods, benchmarks, and leaderboards. It supports the existence of a distinct multilingual-disparity axis, though as a secondary-source review it offers taxonomy and resource aggregation rather than new measurements of the gap.

papers.title: A survey of multilingual large language models
papers.finding: This survey of multilingual LLMs organizes the field around multilingual alignment and explicitly frames cross-lingual performance imbalance — strong results in high-resource languages versus weak coverage of low-resource ones — as a core open challenge motivating dedicated methods, benchmarks, and leaderboards. It supports the existence of a distinct multilingual-disparity axis, though as a secondary-source review it offers taxonomy and resource aggregation rather than new measurements of the gap.

papers.title: Multilingual Large Language Models do not comprehend all natural languages to equal degrees
papers.finding: Prompting 3 LLMs across 12 languages from 5 families, the authors find measurable cross-language performance fluctuations in comprehension, with models falling short of human baselines to differing degrees by language, and they tie variation to tokenization, training-data size, language distance, and WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD data origin. The paper complicates the naive framing — English is not the top language and is systematically beaten by several Romance languages, including lower-resource ones, and typologically diverse languages show 'remarkable accuracy' — but this refines rather than refutes the existence of language-dependent disparity worth measuring.

papers.title: UA-Code-Bench: A Competitive Programming Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Code Generation in Ukrainian
papers.finding: UA-Code-Bench evaluates 13 leading models on 500 Ukrainian-language competitive programming problems and finds even top models (o3, GPT-5) solve only ~half, which the authors attribute in part to the challenge of prompting in a low-resource natural language. This supports tracking cross-language performance gaps on identical task types, though the paper lacks a matched English control set, so the evidence for a language-specific disparity (rather than task difficulty) is indirect.

papers.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models Across Multilingual and Obfuscated Attack Scenarios
papers.finding: Evaluating six frontier LLMs under adversarial prompts, the authors find non-English prompts consistently yield higher malicious-compliance rates than identical English prompts, evidence that safety alignment is unevenly distributed across languages. The finding is about safety robustness rather than task accuracy, and the paper's primary focus is prompt injection, so it supports the multilingual-disparity capability only indirectly.

papers.title: The role of artificial intelligence in medical education: an evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs) on the Turkish Medical Specialty Training Entrance Exam
papers.finding: Four LLMs were tested on 240 Turkish medical specialty exam questions, with accuracy ranging from 88.75% (GPT-4) to 50% (Command R+). The study is framed around whether models work "in languages other than English," but without a parallel English condition it cannot isolate a language-driven gap — the spread across models could equally reflect general capability differences. It shows some models handle a non-English professional exam well, which is weakly consistent with the capability being model-dependent rather than either confirming or refuting a systematic high/low-resource disparity.

capabilities.label: Keeping outputs and solution paths diverse
capabilities.summary: Covers mode collapse, entropy decline, and repeated attempts retreading the same strategy after sampling, fine-tuning, or RL; excludes single- answer accuracy and stylistic variety alone.

best_supports.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
best_supports.finding: The paper documents that RLVR training drives policy entropy collapse, narrowing reasoning coverage and degrading pass@k at large k, and proposes weak-model prefix guidance as a non-parametric perturbation to preserve generative diversity. This treats diversity loss from RL as a measurable, distinct failure mode separate from single-answer accuracy.

papers.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
papers.finding: The paper documents that RLVR training drives policy entropy collapse, narrowing reasoning coverage and degrading pass@k at large k, and proposes weak-model prefix guidance as a non-parametric perturbation to preserve generative diversity. This treats diversity loss from RL as a measurable, distinct failure mode separate from single-answer accuracy.

papers.title: On Epistemic Diversity in Large Language Models
papers.finding: Formalizes 'epistemic diversity' as the range of valid answers, explanations, and reasoning routes an LLM exposes, arguing that accuracy and alignment metrics miss a distinct failure mode in which a model gives correct answers while narrowing users' access to alternative valid responses — direct conceptual and evaluative support for tracking output/solution-path diversity separately from single-answer correctness.

capabilities.label: Changing what a person believes or decides
capabilities.summary: How effectively a model shifts a person's beliefs or choices in conversation, relative to a human doing the same; the risk is the flip side of the capability, a system that can talk its operators out of constraining it.

best_supports.title: On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4
best_supports.finding: Preregistered 2x2x3 online debate experiment (N=900) measured post-debate opinion change with a direct human comparator. GPT-4 with access to participants' sociodemographic data was more persuasive than human opponents in 64.4% of non-tied pairs (+81.2% odds of higher post-debate agreement, 95% CI [+26.0%, +160.7%], p<0.01), while humans given the same personalization data showed no comparable gain. This is exactly the construct the capability describes: a measured shift in human belief caused by model output, benchmarked against humans, with personalization as the driver.

papers.title: On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4
papers.finding: Preregistered 2x2x3 online debate experiment (N=900) measured post-debate opinion change with a direct human comparator. GPT-4 with access to participants' sociodemographic data was more persuasive than human opponents in 64.4% of non-tied pairs (+81.2% odds of higher post-debate agreement, 95% CI [+26.0%, +160.7%], p<0.01), while humans given the same personalization data showed no comparable gain. This is exactly the construct the capability describes: a measured shift in human belief caused by model output, benchmarked against humans, with personalization as the driver.

papers.title: The levers of political persuasion with conversational artificial intelligence
papers.finding: Across three preregistered experiments with 76,977 participants and 19 LLMs on 707 political issues, conversational AI produced measurable shifts in participants' policy attitudes, with persuasiveness varying systematically by post-training (up to +51%) and prompting (up to +27%) far more than by personalization or model scale. Information-dense, claim-heavy strategies drove the gains, and the same manipulations that raised persuasiveness lowered factual accuracy across 466,769 checked claims — direct evidence that model-induced belief change is a real, manipulable, separately measurable property with a distinct accuracy trade-off.

papers.title: The potential of generative AI for personalized persuasion at scale
papers.finding: Across four studies (seven sub-studies, N=1788), messages generated by ChatGPT and personalized to recipients' psychological profiles (personality traits, political ideology, moral foundations) produced significantly greater attitude and behavioral-intention shifts than non-personalized LLM messages, across marketing and political/climate domains, even from a single short prompt naming the target dimension. This is a direct measurement of model output changing human beliefs and choices, showing persuasion is measurable and scalable; the main gap relative to the proposed scope is the absence of a human-persuader comparator (the baseline is non-personalized LLM text).

papers.title: Evaluating the persuasive influence of political microtargeting with large language models
papers.finding: In a preregistered RCT with 8,587 participants, GPT-4-generated messages shifted stated support on political issues by up to 12 percentage points, demonstrating measurable model-caused belief change; microtargeting on individual demographic/political data added no significant lift over generic messages (4.83 vs 6.20 pp, p=0.226), locating the capability in generic message quality rather than personalization.

papers.title: How persuasive is AI-generated propaganda?
papers.finding: In a preregistered survey experiment with US respondents, GPT-3-generated propaganda articles significantly increased agreement with the propaganda theses relative to control, and with light human prompt editing or output curation matched the persuasiveness of original human-written foreign propaganda. This is a direct measurement of model-caused belief change against a human comparator, exactly the construct the capability describes.

capabilities.label: Planning a sequence of actions before acting
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can lay out an ordered set of steps toward a goal, with the dependencies right, before or instead of executing them; distinct from carrying the plan out.

best_supports.title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Task Planning
best_supports.finding: SayPlan evaluates LLM-generated task plans in large 3D scene graphs (up to 3 floors, 36 rooms, 140 assets) by scoring plan correctness and executability against expert plans, separately from robot execution. Plans are checked by a scene graph simulator for infeasible actions and revised through iterative replanning, showing that plan validity is a measurable property that improves markedly with grounded feedback and semantic search over the environment representation — treating plan construction and revision as a distinct target of measurement from carrying the plan out.

papers.title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Task Planning
papers.finding: SayPlan evaluates LLM-generated task plans in large 3D scene graphs (up to 3 floors, 36 rooms, 140 assets) by scoring plan correctness and executability against expert plans, separately from robot execution. Plans are checked by a scene graph simulator for infeasible actions and revised through iterative replanning, showing that plan validity is a measurable property that improves markedly with grounded feedback and semantic search over the environment representation — treating plan construction and revision as a distinct target of measurement from carrying the plan out.

papers.title: Safety Aware Task Planning via Large Language Models in Robotics
papers.finding: SAFER evaluates LLM-generated robotic task plans for safety violations (via an LLM-as-a-Judge metric) before/alongside execution, treating plan quality as a measurable object separate from execution success. It shows base LLM planners produce plans that prioritize task completion over risk mitigation, and that a critic agent revising plans under safety constraints reduces violations while preserving efficiency — evidence that plan generation and revision under new constraints is a distinct, measurable capability. Weight is limited because the paper is a framework proposal with small-scale robotics evaluation and the safety framing entangles planning with goal-conflict-safety and embodied control.

papers.title: LightPlanner: Unleashing the Reasoning Capabilities of Lightweight Large Language Models in Task Planning
papers.finding: LightPlanner trains a 1.5B model to produce robot task plans as parameterized function calls with hierarchical reasoning over goal consistency and parameter validity, and reports higher task success than ReAct baselines (+14.9% on spatial semantic reasoning tasks), treating plan generation quality as the measured object. Evidence is a method paper with a self-built benchmark (LightPlan-40k) rather than a clean diagnostic of plan validity, and success rates are partly execution-confounded, so it is supportive but weak.

capabilities.label: Finding what matters in a large codebase
capabilities.summary: Whether an agent can locate the files, symbols and call paths relevant to a task in a repository too large to read, and avoid editing the wrong place; the failure is a plausible patch in the wrong file.

best_supports.title: LocAgent: Graph-Guided LLM Agents for Code Localization
best_supports.finding: LocAgent isolates code localization as its own task: it parses repositories into directed heterogeneous graphs (files, classes, functions linked by imports, invocations, inheritance) and measures file-, module- and function-level localization accuracy separately from patch generation, reporting up to 92.7% file-level accuracy. Because localization is scored directly and the graph-based navigation tools are ablated against conventional search, the paper treats finding the right place in a large repo as a distinct, measurable skill whose quality gates downstream fixes — better localization lifts GitHub issue resolution by ~12% at Pass@10, and a fine-tuned 32B model matches proprietary SOTA at ~86% lower cost, showing the bottleneck is navigation rather than raw code ability.

papers.title: LocAgent: Graph-Guided LLM Agents for Code Localization
papers.finding: LocAgent isolates code localization as its own task: it parses repositories into directed heterogeneous graphs (files, classes, functions linked by imports, invocations, inheritance) and measures file-, module- and function-level localization accuracy separately from patch generation, reporting up to 92.7% file-level accuracy. Because localization is scored directly and the graph-based navigation tools are ablated against conventional search, the paper treats finding the right place in a large repo as a distinct, measurable skill whose quality gates downstream fixes — better localization lifts GitHub issue resolution by ~12% at Pass@10, and a fine-tuned 32B model matches proprietary SOTA at ~86% lower cost, showing the bottleneck is navigation rather than raw code ability.

papers.title: RepoGraph: Enhancing AI Software Engineering with Repository-level Code Graph
papers.finding: RepoGraph builds a repository-wide code graph of symbol definitions and invocation edges and plugs it into four existing SWE-bench systems (both agentic and procedural pipelines), improving resolve rates across all of them and setting a new open-source state of the art; the module is a pure navigation/context-retrieval addition rather than a change to the patching model, so the gains isolate 'finding the right place in the repo' as a separable bottleneck from writing the edit. Analyses of localization quality and transfer to CrossCodeEval reinforce that repo-scale context retrieval is the limiting factor.

papers.title: OrcaLoca: An LLM Agent Framework for Software Issue Localization
papers.finding: OrcaLoca treats issue localization as a distinct, separately-measurable task: it reports function match rate on SWE-bench Lite (65.33%, open-source SOTA) independently of patch generation, and shows that swapping in better localization raises an existing framework's resolved rate by 6.33 points. Ablations over its navigation machinery (priority-based scheduling, action decomposition with relevance scoring, distance-aware context pruning) isolate which search mechanisms drive localization accuracy, supporting the claim that finding the right file/function is a separable bottleneck from editing code.

papers.title: Issue Localization via LLM-Driven Iterative Code Graph Searching
papers.finding: COSIL measures function-level issue localization on SWE-bench Lite/Verified as a standalone task, reporting Top-1 accuracy (43.3%/44.6% with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B) separately from patch generation, and shows that swapping in better localization raises Agentless's resolution rate by 2.98-30.5%. The paper also ablates navigation machinery specifically — the two-phase module-to-function call-graph search, a pruner that filters irrelevant search directions, and a reflection mechanism for malformed tool interactions — evidencing that locating the right file/function is a separable bottleneck from editing, and that prior methods fail by searching too narrowly (only issue-mentioned files) or too broadly (whole repo).

papers.title: SweRank: Software Issue Localization with Code Ranking
papers.finding: SweRank isolates issue localization — mapping a natural-language bug report to the specific files, classes and functions to edit — as a standalone task with its own benchmarks (SWE-Bench-Lite, LocBench) and metrics, showing it can be measured and improved independently of patch generation. The finding that a retrieve-and-rerank pipeline trained on SweLoc beats agentic systems built on Claude-3.5 indicates that localization is a separable bottleneck rather than a byproduct of general coding skill, and that off-the-shelf code retrievers tuned for query-to-code search underperform on verbose, failure-descriptive issue queries.

capabilities.label: Using what was retrieved, and only that
capabilities.summary: Given relevant passages in context, whether a model actually uses them, prefers them over its own prior when they conflict, and ignores the irrelevant ones; the failure is an answer the passages do not support.

best_supports.title: RAD-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models Capabilities in Retrieval Augmented Dialogues
best_supports.finding: RAD-Bench holds retrieval fixed — providing accurate retrieved contexts alongside multi-turn discriminative questions — and scores whether model responses actually integrate and reason over those passages against reference answers. Evaluated LLMs degrade as additional conditions or constraints accumulate across turns even though the correct context is supplied, showing that using given evidence is a separable failure mode from retrieving it. Evidence is somewhat indirect for the conflict-with-parametric-knowledge and distractor-ignoring aspects of the proposed capability, which the benchmark does not isolate.

papers.title: RAD-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models Capabilities in Retrieval Augmented Dialogues
papers.finding: RAD-Bench holds retrieval fixed — providing accurate retrieved contexts alongside multi-turn discriminative questions — and scores whether model responses actually integrate and reason over those passages against reference answers. Evidence is somewhat indirect for the conflict-with-parametric-knowledge and distractor-ignoring aspects of the proposed capability, which the benchmark does not isolate.

papers.title: Coordinated Semantic Alignment and Evidence Constraints for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Large Language Models
papers.finding: The paper frames "insufficient evidence utilization" as a distinct failure mode of RAG systems, separate from retrieval quality, and proposes an explicit evidence-constraint mechanism that turns retrieved passages from implicit context into a controlling factor on generation, reporting improved factual reliability and verifiability across generation-quality metrics. This treats grounding-in-retrieved-evidence as a separable, improvable target, which supports the capability's existence — but it is a method paper that changes the system rather than holding retrieval fixed and diagnostically measuring whether the model follows the passages, and it does not test conflicts with parametric knowledge or robustness to irrelevant passages. Evidence is reported only as vague 'stable improvements across multiple generation quality metrics' without specified benchmarks, so its evidentiary weight is low.

capabilities.label: Being supervised by something weaker than itself
capabilities.summary: Whether a model's behaviour can be shaped and checked by a supervisor — a person or a weaker model — that cannot do the task as well; the failure is a supervisor that cannot tell a good answer from a convincing one.

capabilities.label: Making design decisions that hold up as a system grows
capabilities.summary: Whether a model can choose structure — module boundaries, interfaces, data flow — that stays maintainable, as opposed to code that passes the tests today; the failure is locally correct code that raises the cost of every later change.

best_supports.title: Do Large Language Models Contain Software Architectural Knowledge? : An Exploratory Case Study with GPT
best_supports.finding: In an exploratory case study, 14 software engineers queried GPT about the architectural knowledge of HDFS and compared answers to a predefined ground truth. GPT showed moderate recall but lower precision, and was weakest precisely on quality-attribute solutions and design rationales — the architectural reasoning behind structure rather than code-level facts. Engineers rated quality and trustworthiness only moderate and concluded expert validation remains necessary. This separates architecture-level design knowledge from working-code generation and shows it is measurable against expert ground truth, though the study is small, single-system, and probes knowledge recall rather than the downstream maintenance cost of model design choices.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Contain Software Architectural Knowledge? : An Exploratory Case Study with GPT
papers.finding: In an exploratory case study, 14 software engineers queried GPT about the architectural knowledge of HDFS and compared answers to a predefined ground truth. GPT showed moderate recall but lower precision, and was weakest precisely on quality-attribute solutions and design rationales — the architectural reasoning behind structure rather than code-level facts. Engineers rated quality and trustworthiness only moderate and concluded expert validation remains necessary. This separates architecture-level design knowledge from working-code generation and shows it is measurable against expert ground truth, though the study is small, single-system, and probes knowledge recall rather than the downstream maintenance cost of model design choices.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Assistants in Software Architecture Design
papers.finding: An IEEE Software-style article arguing LLMs can assist architects in evaluating design concepts, patterns and technologies against quality attributes — treating architectural decision-making as a distinct task from writing working code. It is largely exploratory/positional rather than a measured benchmark, so it establishes the capability as worth tracking without quantifying how well models do.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Software Architecture Design Support in Self-Adaptive Systems: Early Insights from an Exploratory Systematic Review
papers.finding: A work-in-progress systematic review found only four studies using LLMs/GenAI in the architectural design of self-adaptive systems, where LLMs act as augmentative reasoning components across MAPE-K phases. It reports an evidence gap rather than any measurement of whether model-chosen structure holds up as a system grows; trustworthiness and runtime assurance are noted as underexplored.
